segments.text: You play the role of the unnamed protagonist, a former male stripper who aims to becomes the world's best mahjong player. A former mahjong champion sees potential in your play, and offers your choice of his three daughters. The sisters have their doubts, but nonetheless grant the chance to prove yourself in games of strip mahjong. Although he defeats each of them, our protagonist balks at the offer of marriage.

Now that he's become friendly with the sisters, they continue to play against one another. While they know he is the strongest player they have ever seen, he still loses sometimes - perhaps even on purpose in order to show off more than just his gaming skills.

The sisters' aging father believes that the game of mahjong is a simile for life. To be a strong mahjong player is to be a person of incredible strength: physically, mentally, and emotionally. He believes that only an expert mahjong player is worthy of taking one of his daughter's hands in marriage, yet he's saddened by the fact that he's found only one such person thus far, although this player has not shown as much interest in marrying his daughters as he had hoped.

Folowing his championship career, he established a large chain of mahjong gaming halls, but now several of those have reverted to independent ownership. What remains is to be gifted to his future son-in-law.

Youngest of the three sisters, Rumi is not as proficient of a mahjong player as her older sisters, Yumika and Miyabi. She is eager to learn though and vows to someday best them both as well as the protagonist. She wishes for a husband who will let her go shopping anytime she wants, but she knows she's not quite old enough for marriage yet, despite her father's opinion.
She is kidnapped in a plot to undermine her family's near monopoly on mahjong gaming halls. But once she discovers who her captor is, she agrees to play along.

The eldest daughter, Yumika is the strongest mahjong player of the three sisters. Smart and sexy, Yumika is a careful player, practically unbeatable until bested by the protagonist. She's seeking a husband who will support her ambitious goals as a sophisticated businesswoman.

Following Rumi's abduction, Yumika joins the rescue mission. She has her reservations about being too noisy into other people's business but the others disregard her warnings. When it becomes evident to her who has taken Rumi, she remains silent, waiting to see how everything turns out before passing judgement upon others.

The middle sister, Miyabi is perhaps best known for her oversized gold earrings. Despite her propensity to wear less clothing than her sisters, she's actually more embaressed to strip than either of her siblings. As such, she often wears extra accessories when playing strip mahjong. Miyabi tends to gloat when she wins. She's seeking a husband who will provide her with a life of luxury.

After Rumi's kidnapping, Miyabi is the most willing of the group to take risks, such as trespassing, thus offsetting the more restrictive influence of her older sister, Yumika. In the end, this trait pays off more often than not.
